children: Britain’s competition regulator is considering requiring Google
to make it easier for users to choose and switch between search services, including through Google’s Chrome browser, as part of efforts to promote competition in online search.

The Competition and Markets Authority, or CMA, has proposed that Google display choice screens at key access points, including Android devices and Chrome, and make it easier for users to change their default search service.
The CMA is also considering whether choice screens should include generative AI services such as OpenAI's ChatGPT
, and Perplexity, alongside traditional search engines.
A final decision on the user-choice requirement has not yet been made.
The CMA has designated Google as "strategic market status" in general search services in 2025.

asked Google to improve transparency and fairness in how search results are ranked and to allow users to port their search data to authorized third parties such as rewards platforms or companies offering personalized offers or discount codes.
Google already operates search choice screens in the European Economic Area under the EU's Digital Markets Act, including in Chrome on desktop and iOS.

title: UK watchdog wants Google to offer broader search choices, including AI
